subject: Bridging incentives & migration stopgap proposal
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara@crowdedge.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging incentives & migration stopgap proposal

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I put together a short stopgap proposal that addresses the three blockers you mentioned: 1) short-term unit economics while you validate runtime parity, 2) egress exposure during data export, and 3) a low-friction onboarding window for engineers.

High level offer (summary):
- 60-day pilot period with a 25% onboarding credit applied to token usage for the first 30 days.
- One-time migration credit bucket: $120,000 applied to invoices or pre-paid credits (customer choice).
- Free egress up to 2TB within the first 90 days; incremental egress billed at discounted rate.
- Dedicated onboarding support: 3 sessions with an engineer + prioritized queue for runtime tuning.

Attached: CrowdEdge_Redwood_Stopgap_Proposal.pdf (proposal), CE_Migration_Cost_Workup.xlsx (line-item workup).

If this looks reasonable, can we get procurement and legal on a quick 30-minute call next week to lock terms? Proposed times: Tue 11/2 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 11/3 8:30-9:00 PT.

I can loop in Markus for an approval note if you want this to be firmed up ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

--- Attachment stubs: CrowdEdge_Redwood_Stopgap_Proposal.pdf (PDF), CE_Migration_Cost_Workup.xlsx (Excel)


From: Sara Holt <sara@crowdedge.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: CrowdEdge Procurement <procurement@crowdedge.com>, legal@crowdedge.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging incentives & migration stopgap proposal

Jasmine —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear worksheet. A few things procurement/legal want clarified before we schedule:

1) Can you map the $120k migration credit to a concrete discount schedule? Procurement wants to see runway: e.g., how many months of usage this offsets at our current consumption (we're roughly $45k/mo today).
2) Egress: free up to 2TB is helpful, but we need an upper bound scenario. If we end up exporting 10TB, what's the incremental cost?
3) SLA and rollback: our legal asks that any one-off credits or pilot terms not create open-ended SLAs or extended uptime guarantees without a corresponding support commitment.

We also received a competing commercial from CloudRamp that includes a 3-month credit and a 30% onboarding discount. I'm not asking you to match line-for-line, but we need a clear, defensible package that reduces our migration risk and the conversion lift for our infra team.

Can you get me a single-page comparison that shows Redwood vs CloudRamp on total cost over a 6-month horizon and the operational commitments?

Best,
Sara
Director, Cloud Ops — CrowdEdge


From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara@crowdedge.com>
Cc: CrowdEdge Procurement <procurement@crowdedge.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging incentives & migration stopgap proposal

Sara —

Thanks — totally reasonable asks. I updated the workup and added a short comparison tab that projects costs at current usage, 2x, and 4x consumption over six months (see CE_Migration_Cost_Workup.xlsx). Quick answers inline: 

- $120k credit mapping: at your current run-rate (~$45k/mo), the credit covers ~2.6 months of usage. If consumption doubles, it covers ~1.3 months. The sheet has the month-by-month net spend after credits.
- Egress worst-case: after the first 2TB free, incremental egress is $0.08/GB for months 0–3, stepping to $0.12/GB thereafter. So 10TB total (8TB beyond free) would be ~$655 for months 0–3 tiered portion + remainder at standard discounted rate — full math in the sheet.
- SLA/rollback: we will not change our standard SLA language as part of a stopgap. What we can do is include a documented rollback runbook and a 30-day targeted remediation window with engineering hours covered as part of the migration credit. Legal sign-off needed for any ad-hoc SLA addendum.

If that framing looks acceptable, I'll ping Markus to sign-off on a binding stopgap (he's cc'd) and ask CS to sketch the 30/60/90-day onboarding milestones.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Hi all —

Reviewed Jasmine's memo and the cost workup. I'm comfortable approving a firm stopgap structure to close this quarter with the following commitments: 

- One-time migration credit: $120,000 (as proposed).
- Temporary discounted run-rate: 20% off list for the first 3 billed months after pilot (applies after the onboarding credit is exhausted).
- Egress protection: 2TB free + capped egress credit of $30,000 beyond the free tier to cover high-export scenarios during the migration window.
- Onboarding acceleration: priority engineering hours (up to 40 hours) and a named CS lead.

Legal constraints: provide this as a 12-month limited commercial concession; no changes to core SLA language. Grace — can you draft the 30/60/90 runbook and estimated onboarding timeline so procurement can evaluate go/no-go?

Markus
SVP, Sales Operations
